h: Even the Castaway Remains Bound to the Root

p: וְאַרְבָּעָה אֲנָשִׁים הָיוּ מְצוֹרָעִים וְגוֹ׳ (מְלָכִים ב ז, ג)
"And there were four men who were metzora'im," etc. (Melachim II 7:3).
For the theme of this parshah,
"the law of the metzora on the day of his purification,"
having gone out of the category of
by which all of Yisrael have a share
And in the Mishnah (Sanhedrin 10:2) are counted
וְהֵם ז׳ כְּנֶגֶד ז׳ מִדּוֹת תַּחְתּוֹנִיּוֹת
and they are seven, corresponding to the seven lower attributes;
And they are seven including Bilam,
were like grass of the field before them"
corresponding to the years of his reign;
Doeg was "the mightiest of the shepherds,"
and they too were great in Torah
And of Gechazi it also says
that he was mighty in Torah.
that he pushed the Sages away from before him.
And this is according to what I heard
in the name of a certain holy Rav,
who said, regarding what they said (Berachos 28a),
who was not the same inside as outside?
And he said that it was an angel;
that whoever is not the same inside as outside
whoever was not the same inside as outside
and once this statement was annulled,
his power was to push away the Sages,
whoever was not the same inside as outside;
and he was struck with tzaraas,
And pride corresponds to the husk of Amalek,
"'A man's pride will bring him low' (Mishlei 29:23):
And Amalek is sent away entirely
for converts are not accepted from Amalek
and Tanchuma, end of Parshas Teitzei).
And so the metzora is sent away
And from what is written (Melachim II 5:27),
"And the tzaraas of Naaman shall cling to you
that he would be sent away forever
that he has no share in the World to Come,
for he went out of the category of
from which it is learned of all Yisrael
that they have a share in the World to Come.
And we learned in this parshah
that even souls such as these
and he shall be brought to the Kohen,"
this is the Holy One, blessed be He
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג מט, ב)
And we read as the haftarah of the four metzora'im,
of whom it says in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 107b)
that they were Gechazi and his three sons;
and from what is written, "you and your seed forever,"
it is implied that his seed
and nevertheless through them came about
that at the root they have a remedy,
who are of the seed of Yaakov
that they have a share in the World to Come
for everyone who is of the seed of Yaakov
is bound to the root of Hashem Yisbarach,
